answer_q: What is an AI readiness assessment?
answer: An AI readiness assessment is a structured review of whether a business has the data, systems, processes, skills, governance and budget needed to adopt AI successfully. It produces a readiness score, the gaps to close and the AI opportunities that are realistic to pursue first.
body:
Why assess readiness first

Most failed AI projects don’t fail because the AI was bad. They fail because the data was scattered, the process wasn’t understood, staff weren’t brought along or nobody owned the result. A readiness assessment surfaces those problems before you invest, so your first AI project lands on solid ground. It also stops you over-investing: sometimes the right next step is a simple data clean-up or a policy, not a new tool.

You can get a quick indication with our free one-minute online readiness check. The full assessment goes much deeper, with interviews, system reviews and a written report.

The six areas we assess

AreaWhat we look at
DataWhere information lives, how complete and accurate it is, and whether it can be accessed securely
SystemsYour software, integrations, APIs and any legacy tools that limit automation
ProcessesHow consistent key workflows are, where time goes and which steps are documented
People and skillsCurrent AI use, confidence, training needs and attitudes across the team
Governance and privacyPolicies, accountability, privacy practices and how staff use public AI tools today
Strategy and budgetBusiness goals, leadership alignment and the investment available

Each area receives a score from one to five, with evidence and a short explanation, so the result is easy to share with owners or a board.

How the assessment works

  1. Kick-off: we agree scope, the teams involved and the systems to review.
  2. Interviews: short sessions with leaders and the people who do the work.
  3. System and data review: we look at your key systems and sample data quality, with read-only access where possible.
  4. Policy review: we check privacy, security and AI usage practices against Australian guidance.
  5. Report and debrief: you receive scores, findings, gaps and recommendations, and we walk you through them.

What you get

  • An overall AI readiness score and a score for each of the six areas
  • The three AI opportunities best suited to your current readiness
  • A gap list with practical fixes, effort and indicative costs in AUD
  • Risks to manage, including privacy and staff-use risks
  • A recommended 30-day action plan

Readiness levels and what they mean

Explorer

Information is mostly in email, spreadsheets or people’s heads. The best next steps are getting key data into cloud systems, writing an AI usage policy and trying one low-risk automation.

Ready to pilot

Core systems are in the cloud and the team is curious. A focused pilot on one high-volume workflow should show results within a month.

Ready to scale

Systems are connected, data is reasonably clean and governance exists. You are ready for an AI roadmap across several departments.

Built on Australian standards

Our governance and privacy questions draw on the Australian Government’s Guidance for AI Adoption and the OAIC’s guidance on privacy and commercially available AI products. That makes the report useful evidence if clients, insurers or auditors ask how you manage AI.

After the assessment

Some clients act on the report themselves. Others ask us to close the gaps or deliver the first opportunity through AI automation or AI agents. There is no obligation either way. If your team needs skills more than systems, see AI training for teams.

Questions the assessment answers

  • Which of our processes are realistic to automate this year, and which aren’t yet?
  • Is our data good enough for AI, and what would it take to fix it?
  • Are staff already sharing client information with public AI tools?
  • Do our current systems have the integrations AI needs?
  • What budget and internal time should we set aside for a first project?
  • Who should own AI in the business?

Clear answers to these questions save money. They stop you buying tools your data can’t support, and they give you a defensible plan to share with owners, staff and clients.

Who it suits

The assessment suits businesses of 10 to 500 people that are curious about AI but unsure where to start, organisations whose staff are already using AI tools informally, and leadership teams that need an objective baseline before approving a budget. It is often the first step before a full AI strategy.

Many clients repeat the assessment after six to twelve months to measure progress and reset priorities.
faqs: How long does an AI readiness assessment take?
Most assessments take one to two weeks, depending on the number of teams and systems involved. Interviews usually need 30 to 45 minutes per person.
What is the difference between the free online check and the full assessment?

The free online check gives a quick indicative score from six questions. The full assessment includes interviews, system and data reviews, policy checks and a written report with costed recommendations.
Do you need access to our systems?
Read-only access to key systems helps us assess data quality accurately, but we can also work from screen-share walkthroughs and sample exports if you prefer.
What does an AI readiness assessment cost?
Cost depends on the size of the business and the number of systems in scope. We give a fixed price in AUD after a free 30-minute audit.
